seo_title: Cost of Living in Da Nang 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Da Nang per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Vietnam's rising capital of digital nomads: a long beach, a warm sea year-round, very low prices and a convenient visa. The city blends a resort pace with a developed IT infrastructure.
pros: The longest city beach in the region (My Khe)
Very low prices: housing, food and transport
A growing community of digital nomads and founders
Close to Hoi An, the Hai Van Pass and national parks
Stable 4G/5G and a developed infrastructure for remote work
cons: Typhoon season from September to November
Difficulties with a long-term visa for Russian citizens
Getting around is hard without a motorbike or car
A language barrier outside the tourist zone

best_places.name: My Khe Beach
best_places.description: 30 km of white sand along the city's eastern shore — one of the best city beaches in the world.

best_places.name: An Thuong
best_places.description: An expat quarter by the sea: Western cafés, yoga studios, coworkings and a large international community.

best_places.name: Surf Coworking Da Nang
best_places.description: The main space for remote workers, with meeting rooms, events and a rooftop terrace.

best_places.name: Son Tra Peninsula
best_places.description: A wild reserve in the north: beaches, viewpoints and a giant Buddha statue.

visa_steps.title: E-Visa
visa_steps.description: A 90-day electronic visa for Russian citizens, arranged online in 3 days.

visa_steps.title: DN business visa
visa_steps.description: Through an invitation from a Vietnamese company. Valid for up to 1 year with extension.

visa_steps.title: Tax registration
visa_steps.description: For working for Western companies — via an MST (tax code). Issued at the local branch of the General Department of Taxation.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Vietcombank, Techcombank, VPBank open accounts for foreigners with a DN visa and a lease contract.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Long-term rentals (from 6 months) — through local agents or Facebook groups. The lease is registered with the police.

faq.question: When is the best season in Da Nang?
faq.answer: From March to August — dry and warm. September–November is the season of typhoons and rain.

faq.question: How is banking in Da Nang?
faq.answer: Harder than in Thailand: you need a DN visa and a lease contract. Opening an account is almost impossible for tourists.

faq.question: Where to live in Da Nang?
faq.answer: An Thuong — expats and the beach. The Han River — modern complexes. Son Tra Peninsula — villas and quiet.

faq.question: Can I relocate with children to Da Nang?
faq.answer: Singapore International School Da Nang is the main international school. Fees start from $12,000 a year.

faq.question: What transport is there in Da Nang?
faq.answer: Renting a motorbike ($50–70 a month) is the main way to get around. Grab taxis are cheap.

faq.question: How is the internet in Da Nang?
faq.answer: Fibre at 100+ Mbps for 600 rubles a month, mobile 4G everywhere. Perfect for remote work.

reviews.text: I'm wintering in Da Nang for the second year: a place by the sea for 25,000 rubles, coffee for 80, surfing every day. The downside is the visa every 3 months — I do a visa run to Thailand.
I moved from Bangkok: quieter, cheaper, the ocean instead of that gulf-like sea. I work remotely and pay tax in Russia. Da Nang is Vietnam-lite without the megacity noise.
